title: Build a small leakage-resistant gap forecast benchmark

blocks.text: Competing forecasts use identical origins; every forecast cell contributes to pooled WAPE. The task is: Benchmark seasonal-naive and trailing-mean forecasts under the SAME rolling origins. Skip origins lacking max(season,window) history; return records and pooled forecast-cell WAPE for each model. Overlapping horizons count each forecast cell separately. Data deduplication/as-of joins are preceding exercises, not hidden in this benchmark core.

The inputs are `series`, `cutoffs`, `horizon`, `season`, `window`. Keep their roles separate while you trace the solution. The animation follows the supplied implementation, so every highlighted operation connects to code you can inspect.

blocks.text: Read each symbol as a value with a specific axis, time, rank, token, or state role. The code must preserve those roles. A compact formula does not remove the validation, masking, boundary, or state rules in the prompt.

Before following the implementation, identify the output's shape and meaning. Then identify which input values can affect one selected output. This gives you a testable mental model before the code adds implementation detail.
What changes in the boundary case

Change one input at the edge of the stated contract and trace where the behavior changes. Use the Trace control to switch between the normal path and this boundary focus. The algorithm does not get permission to invent an unstated fallback.

A useful test changes one condition while holding the remaining inputs fixed. Compare the output shape, state transition, valid edges, selected tokens, or returned status. This isolates the reason for the change.
A diagram can show data moving and still hide a wrong contract. Check the mask direction, reduction axis, update order, and ownership of persistent state against the prompt.
